note: Story arcs for the director (apps/engine/src/core/story.ts). Each seeded conflict moves simmer -> incident -> confront -> decision -> aftermath. Text here is pressure and stakes, never dialogue: the LLM writes what people actually say and the decider's choice is made by the brain (resolveArc).

arcs.title: The bakery loan

incident.text: A third loan payment on Okafor's Bakery falls due today and the till is ₡120 short.

confront.note: Tunde has noticed Mira counting the till twice. Today he asks her straight out what is wrong with the money.

decision.question: Does Neil call in the bakery loan, extend it once more on his own word, or quietly cover the gap himself?

options.fact: The bank has called in the bakery loan. The Okafors must find ₡600 within the week or lose the ovens.
Neil Ashdown extended the bakery loan by a month on his own signature, against bank policy.
Someone paid the bakery's missed instalment in cash. Neil Ashdown won't say who.

arcs.aftermath: The bakery loan is settled one way or another. Live with the result: the money, the pride, and who knew what.

arcs.title: The rent cap

incident.text: Marcus Vale has posted new rents on Gull Lane: up ₡10 a week from next month. Four tenants are already behind.

confront.note: The tenants want a rent-cap petition signed by the weekend. Jay is collecting names door to door; Marcus is visiting the same doors.

decision.question: Does Mayor Ingrid put the rent cap to the council, bury the petition, or broker a private deal with her brother-in-law?

options.fact: The mayor has put a rent cap to the council, against her own brother-in-law.
The rent-cap petition sits unread on the mayor's desk. The tenants know it.
Marcus Vale has agreed to delay the Gull Lane rise until spring after a private talk with the mayor.

arcs.aftermath: The rent question has an answer for now. Tenants and landlord adjust to it, and everyone remembers who stood where.

arcs.title: Two fishers, one buyer

incident.text: Leo Petrov saw Devendra Rao's scale tip before a single fish touched it. He has told Chen.

confront.note: Chen has a year of price slips. Today the fishers talk about selling together, as a cooperative, instead of one by one to Devendra.

decision.question: Does Devendra raise his prices to keep the fishers, threaten them, or let the cooperative happen and sell for them?

options.fact: Devendra Rao now pays fishers a crown more a crate. He says it was always the plan.
Devendra Rao told the fishers that anyone who joins a cooperative will not sell a single crate at the market again.
The fishers and Devendra Rao shook hands on a shared price board at the Fish Market.

arcs.aftermath: The fish price fight has settled. People adjust their days, their margins and their grudges to it.

arcs.title: Walter vs the doctor

incident.text: Walter Finch stood up in the Anchor last night and said out loud that Dr Achebe killed his wife.

confront.note: Grace Achebe has heard what Walter said. Today she wants her husband to answer it, and Samuel wants to be left alone.

decision.question: Does Dr Achebe visit Walter and admit his part, keep silent, or ask the council to stop the slander?

options.fact: Dr Achebe sat with Walter Finch for an hour. Walter has not said a word against him since.
Dr Achebe will not discuss Walter Finch. The tavern talk goes on.
Dr Achebe has asked the council to warn Walter Finch about slander.

arcs.aftermath: Something has shifted between the doctor and the widower. The town notices who sits where.

arcs.title: The brothers and the licence

incident.text: A crate of Kowalski beer was delivered to the back door of Café Moreno, labelled for the café.

confront.note: Jonah now knows his brother is supplying the café that wants to compete with his tavern. Today he goes to the brewery.

decision.question: Does Wojtek keep supplying the café, back out for his brother, or offer Jonah a better price too?

options.fact: Wojtek Kowalski will keep supplying Café Moreno. The brothers are not speaking.
Wojtek Kowalski has stopped supplying Café Moreno. Rosa is furious.
Wojtek Kowalski now sells to both the Anchor and the café, and gave his brother the lower price.

arcs.aftermath: The brewery has picked its side, or refused to. The brothers live with it.

arcs.title: Jay for mayor

incident.text: Jay Whitlock pinned a hand-written notice to the town hall door: he is standing for mayor.

confront.note: Someone has noticed that Jay has money though he has no job. Yusuf is asked about it at the garage.

decision.question: Does Osman admit he has been paying Jay secretly, stop paying him, or keep quiet and keep paying?

options.fact: Osman Kaya admitted at the garage that he has been paying Jay Whitlock since the firing, out of guilt.
Jay Whitlock's mystery money has stopped. He is counting coins again.
Nobody can say where Jay Whitlock's money comes from, and the rumour has reached the Herald.

effects.gossip: Jay Whitlock has money from somewhere and won't say where

arcs.aftermath: Jay's campaign has a new shape. People who were neutral now have an opinion.

arcs.title: The boundary stone

incident.text: The boundary stone between the Lindqvist and Haddad fields has moved again, and Fatima's channel is dry.

confront.note: Gus Ferreira has seen Per and Fatima at the fence at dusk. He mentions it to Anna, casually.

decision.question: Does Per tell his mother about Fatima and the stone, keep hiding it, or quietly open the water to Fatima's field?

options.fact: Per Lindqvist told his mother he is with Fatima Haddad, and that his late father moved the boundary stone.
Per Lindqvist denies there is anything between him and Fatima Haddad. Nobody quite believes him.
Water is running in the Haddad channel again. The Lindqvist sluice was opened in the night.

arcs.aftermath: The field line, the water and the secret have moved. Both farms live with the new fact.

arcs.title: Zara's way out

incident.text: Teodor Ilić's city job letter fell out of his coat at the bakery. Zara read it before he could pick it up.

confront.note: Zara is weighing leaving with Teodor. Rafa and Felix both want to tell her how they feel before it's too late.

decision.question: Does Zara go to the city with Teodor, stay for her mother's bakery, or tell everyone she is leaving on her own?

options.fact: Zara Okafor will go to the city with Teodor Ilić next month.
Zara Okafor has turned down the city. She says the bakery needs her.
Zara Okafor is leaving Solmere in the spring, alone, and will not say for where.

arcs.aftermath: Zara's choice is made. The young people of Solmere rearrange themselves around it.

arcs.title: The festival money

incident.text: The town accounts are due for posting. Aylin Demir finds the festival overspend of ₡2,100 still hidden in the harbour line.

confront.note: Priya Nair has the figures from a source. She asks the mayor and the clerk for a comment before she prints.

decision.question: Does Mayor Ingrid publish the true accounts herself, blame the clerk, or ask Priya to hold the story until after the election?

options.fact: Mayor Ingrid Halvorsen published the true accounts: ₡2,100 of harbour money paid for the festival.
The mayor says the festival overspend was a clerk's error. Aylin Demir says otherwise.
Priya Nair was asked to hold the festival money story until after the election.

effects.gossip: the mayor tried to stop the Herald printing something about the festival money

arcs.aftermath: The festival money is out in the open, or nearly. Trust in the town hall has moved.

arcs.title: Two teachers

incident.text: Sigrid Vale kept Arjun Rao in after school for a whole afternoon. Noor Rahman let him out.

confront.note: Parents are taking sides at the school gate. Felix's grandfather and Arjun's father both want a word with the teachers.

decision.question: Does Noor accept the job elsewhere, stay and fight for her way of teaching, or offer Sigrid a truce?

options.fact: Noor Rahman has accepted a teaching post in another town. She leaves at the end of term.
Noor Rahman has asked the council to split the school's classes between the two teachers.
The two teachers agreed: mornings Sigrid's way, afternoons Noor's.

arcs.aftermath: The school has a new rule or a teacher fewer. The children notice first.

arcs.title: Hana's offer

incident.text: Dmitri the postman delivered a second envelope from the city hospital to Hana Kimura. He read the return address, as he does.

confront.note: Dr Achebe has heard Hana might leave. Today he asks her, and she has to decide what to say.

decision.question: Does Hana take the city job, stay if the clinic can pay more, or stay and say nothing?

options.fact: Hana Kimura is leaving the clinic for the city hospital in five weeks.
Hana Kimura will stay at the clinic if the council funds a second nurse's wage.
Hana Kimura has written to turn the city hospital down.

arcs.aftermath: The clinic knows whether it keeps its nurse. Patients and colleagues adjust.

arcs.title: The Net Loft

incident.text: Marcus Vale has made an offer for the Old Net Loft. A boat half-built inside it was seen through the window.

confront.note: Kofi asks Ines Larsson for help to keep the loft; Ines has the money to buy it and has never told anyone.

decision.question: Does Ines buy the Net Loft herself, stay out of it, or lend Kofi the money?

options.fact: Ines Larsson bought the Old Net Loft outright, to everyone's surprise. The boat stays.
The Old Net Loft goes to Marcus Vale for holiday flats. Kofi has a week to move the boat.
Kofi Mensah has bought the Net Loft with a private loan nobody can name.

arcs.aftermath: The loft has an owner and a future. The harbour talks about the boat.

arcs.title: Thursday cards

incident.text: Dolores Quinn lost again at Thursday cards. She is now ₡300 down and Sal wants it by the weekend.

confront.note: Ben Carter, the constable who sits at the game, is asked why he never stops it.

decision.question: Does Sal forgive Dolores's debt, press her for it, or close the game before the constable has to?

options.fact: Sal Romano tore up Dolores Quinn's card debt in front of the table.
Dolores Quinn is selling her late husband's watch to pay a card debt.
There is no more Thursday card game at the Anchor.

arcs.aftermath: Thursday nights are different now. Debts and favours have moved.

arcs.title: Father-in-law

incident.text: Yusuf Demir was refused service at the Anchor by a friend of Jay Whitlock: 'you're the one who sacked him'.

confront.note: Aylin is tired of her husband carrying her father's blame. Today she says so to both of them.

decision.question: Does Osman clear Yusuf's name in public, offer Jay his job back, or let it lie?

options.fact: Osman Kaya told the Anchor that firing Jay Whitlock was his decision, not his son-in-law's.
Jay Whitlock has been offered his old job back at Demir Garage.
Osman Kaya says the garage's business is nobody else's. Yusuf keeps carrying it.

arcs.aftermath: The garage family has spoken, or chosen silence. The street hears either way.

arcs.title: Hamish's will

incident.text: Hamish McBride had the lawyer from the next town round for tea. Agnes witnessed something and won't say what.

confront.note: Marcus Vale makes Hamish a generous offer for the orchard, in cash, today.

decision.question: Does Hamish tell Kofi the orchard is his, sell to Marcus, or keep everyone guessing?

options.fact: Hamish McBride told Kofi Mensah the orchard goes to him. Kofi cried in the cider shed.
Hamish McBride sold the orchard to Marcus Vale, keeping the right to live there.
Hamish McBride turned Marcus Vale down with a joke. Nobody knows who gets the orchard.

arcs.aftermath: The orchard's future is settled or teased. Its trees don't care; the town does.

arcs.title: Back-door fish

incident.text: Gus Ferreira saw Tunde Okafor unloading fish at the back of Café Moreno at midnight.

confront.note: Mira asks Tunde where the extra money in the tin comes from. Devendra is asking around too.

decision.question: Does Tunde stop the back-door sales, tell Mira and keep going, or ask the council to change the market bylaw?

options.fact: Tunde Okafor no longer sells fish to the café at night.
Mira Okafor now knows the extra money came from night sales to the café.
Tunde Okafor has asked the council to let fishers sell direct to cafés.

arcs.aftermath: The night trade is over or out in the open. Market mornings feel different.

arcs.title: The harbour wall contract

incident.text: A winter swell overtopped the old harbour wall and flooded the net store.

confront.note: Elias Brand hears an outside firm has bid for the wall, and that Marcus Vale knows the bidder.

decision.question: Does the mayor give the wall to Brand Carpentry, the outside firm, or put it off again?

options.fact: Brand Carpentry has the harbour wall contract. Work starts after the festival.
The harbour wall goes to an outside firm. Elias Brand says the price was never fair.
The harbour wall is put off again until the town can pay for it.

arcs.aftermath: The wall has a builder, a rival, or another delay. The harbour remembers who promised what.

arcs.title: The reporter and the constable

incident.text: Priya Nair's notebook went missing for an hour at the café. It came back on the table, closed.

confront.note: Ben Carter asks Priya not to run what she has on Marcus's council loan; it would end his job too.

decision.question: Does Priya run the story, drop it for Ben's sake, or trade it to Marcus for something bigger?

options.fact: The Herald will print that Marcus Vale has been lending money to the council.
Priya Nair dropped a story. Ben Carter bought her coffee every day this week.
Priya Nair and Marcus Vale had a long, quiet lunch at the Fontaine Inn.

effects.gossip: Priya Nair had a private lunch with Marcus Vale

arcs.aftermath: The story ran, died, or became leverage. Reporter and constable look at each other differently.

arcs.title: Sunny's father

incident.text: Beatrice Fontaine found an old photograph of a young Marcus Vale with a woman who looks exactly like Sunny Adebayo.

confront.note: Sunny has started asking older people about her mother's summers in Solmere. Sigrid notices her husband avoiding the inn.

decision.question: Does Marcus tell Sunny he is her father, deny it, or tell Sigrid first?

options.fact: Marcus Vale told Sunny Adebayo he is her father.
Marcus Vale told Sunny Adebayo he never knew her mother. Bea knows he is lying.
Sigrid Vale now knows who Sunny Adebayo is. She has not slept at home since.

arcs.aftermath: A family secret has moved. The inn, the Vale house and Sunny's room feel it.

arcs.title: Who knows what

incident.text: Sal Romano and Dmitri the postman were seen comparing notes behind the barber's.

confront.note: Beatrice has realised someone is selling what is said at her inn. She asks around.

decision.question: Does Dmitri stop reading people's post, sell what he knows to Priya, or warn the people involved?

options.fact: Dmitri the postman has promised the chapel he will stop reading people's letters.
Dmitri the postman has been passing what he reads to the Herald.
Dmitri the postman quietly warned three people that their letters had been read.

arcs.aftermath: The town's secret-keepers have shifted alliances. People lower their voices in new places.
